A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ICAL@INO can determine the octant of the atmospheric neutrinos mixing angle θ23 at 3σ level for a neutrino energy threshold of 0.6 GeV and an exposure of 5 × 1024 POT, with the true value of the angle in the first octant.

ICAL@INO can determine the octant of the atmospheric mixing angle θ23 with a significance of 4σ, and measure the deviation from maximal mixing to a precision of 0.02 at 90% confidence level, for the normal mass ordering (NMO) of neutrino mass states.

, ICAL@INO is a powerful experiment to measure the atmospheric neutrino oscillations parameters, and it can probe the octant of the atmospheric mixing angle with a statistical significance of 3 σ at 90 % C. L. with 10 years of exposure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ICAL@INO will be able to measure θ23 with an accuracy better than 2.3 degrees, and will be able to determine the octant of the mixing angle θ23 with a significance of 3.3σ.
the ICAL@INO detector has the potential to determine θ23 to an accuracy of 0.04, and |Δm32|2 to an accuracy of ~1%.

, for the current atmospheric neutrino fluxes, a 50 kt ICAL detector is not sensitive enough to the octant degeneracy, and the sensitivity to the deviation of the mixing angle from maximal mixing is also poor.
